summary: A Mingo County fire lookout site at 1,856 ft, registered in 2017 and listed as gone; no source found describes the site or its history today.

facts.status_note: The register lists the tower as gone; no source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on January 26, 2017; nominated by Brian M. Powell.

evidence.supports: tower listed as gone, Mingo County
evidence.quote: Hells Knob Mingo 37.71539 -82.23078 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1678, WV 69

evidence.supports: number of fire towers in WV, 70 to 100 depending on source
evidence.quote: Depending on the source, the number of fire towers in West Virginia range from 70 to 100.

evidence.supports: state used temporary seasonal staff for its towers
evidence.quote: Although hiring practices varied from state to state, the West Virginia Division of Forestry turned to temporary seasonal employees to staff its towers.

evidence.supports: towers manned in fire season or high danger
evidence.quote: Each tower would be staffed during our fire seasons or other times of high fire danger.

evidence.supports: quoted speaker is a deputy state fire manager
evidence.quote: said Deputy State Fire Manager Jeremy Jones, WV DOF

sources.title: Lookout legacy: Fire towers stand as lofty reminders of West Virginia's firefighting history

corrections.why: The register page misspells the state name as 'Virgnia'; the intended name is West Virginia.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. The register gives location, elevation, registration and nominator, and the FFLOS index marks it gone. Two searches and the register and state pages turned up no build date, staffing, removal date or current condition for this site. Source 3 is the state's general account of its towers and is labelled as general in the story. Coordinates: the register detail page (37.715278, -82.230556) matches the record; the index line (37.71539, -82.23078) is about 20 m away, which is minor. The agency correction is a typo in the register text, so a human should confirm before the record changes.
